newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Permanent sees rosy 1997 with striong housing market.
newsitem.headline: Irish Permanent sees rosy 1997 with striong housing market.

text.p: Financial services group Irish Permanent Plc on Tuesday said performance in January 1997 was ahead on the same time last year and the fundamentals in the Irish housing market looked very promising.

"We have had a very good start to the year," chief executive Roy Douglas told Reuters after the release of 1996 results which showed a rise of almost 15 percent in 1996 pre-tax profits. "Our figures for January are ahead of last year."

Douglas said 1996 had been a good year with profits driven by very robust lending growth. He said residential mortage lending, which accounts for 84 percent of the group's business, grew by 46 percent.
"I expect a very strong housing market in Ireland in 1997 perhaps easing off slightly from the particularly buoyant levels of 1996 ... but strong nevertheless," he said.
Official figures show Ireland's house prices up 15 percent year-on-year to September 1996, and mortgage lending up 16.8 percent year-on-year to December 1996.

Douglas said Irish Permanent was also on the lookout for acquisitions. He said the group has a very healthy balance sheet and is keen to consolidate its position in the market where it has increased its market share to 21 percent from 18 percent in 1995.
Irish Permanent was particularly interested in Ireland's TSB Bank which is governed by a board of trustees and whose main shareholder is the Irish government, he said.
Market sources say Irish Permanent itself is considered a potential takeover target by its largest single shareholder Abbey National Plc.

The UK financial services group took a 9.9 percent share in Irish Permanent when it was floated on the stock market in October 1994 but is constrained from taking major stake in the group until after 1999. ($ = 0.637 Irish Pounds)
